newsitem.title: UK: ISDA calls for clearer rules on euro price sources.
newsitem.headline: ISDA calls for clearer rules on euro price sources.

text.p: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association wants providers of price sources, such as LIBOR, to announce their strategy for the euro by July 31, it said in a report on Wednesday.
"There is an urgent need for price sponsors to announce their plans for the euro transition," ISDA chairman Gay Evans said in a statement.
Evans said markets needed to be able to "effectively start to examine the business, systems and legal implications of the changeover from national currency to euro rates".
European economic and monetary union is scheduled to start on January 1, 1999.
Leading price source sponsors in Europe include the British Bankers Association (BBA), the German Banking Associations (GBA/ZKA)and several central banks.

They provide price sources which are central to derivatives trading, such as the London interbank offered rate (or LIBOR -- the cost of short-term money in a host of currencies as quoted by London-based banks) and the Frankfurt interbank offered rate (FIBOR).
The ISDA report called on the European Monetary Institute to monitor the disappearance of price sources, especially where they were sponsored by central banks.

"There is a strong possibility that a number of national price sources will be disbanded and that a single panel for all (or possibly just part) of the EMU area will come into existence to provide euro quotations," the report said.
"The question remains as to whether, for existing contracts, national currency rates quoted by a national pricing panel could be succeeded by a euro rate quoted by a different panel."
As an example, a French franc/mark swap agreement could depend on PIBOR (Paris IBOR) and FIBOR, two measures which may effectively disappear with the advent of the euro.
The ISDA report also called on market participants generally to submit their views relating to the changeover of price sources.
